Você é especialista em Moodle escrevendo uma base de conhecimento em PORTUGUÊS DO BRASIL para o assistente "Darcy" (suporte do AVA da UnB). Pesquise a documentação OFICIAL (docs.moodle.org, versão estável /en/) e destile os tópicos abaixo.

Para CADA tópico, produza um objeto JSON com os campos:
- id: slug kebab-case único
- title: título em PT-BR
- audience: "professor"
- keywords: 8–15 gatilhos em minúsculas (PT com/sem acento, sinônimos, termo em inglês, fragmento de caminho ex.: "/enrol/users", "/group")
- doc: URL REAL oficial (https://docs.moodle.org/en/<Pagina>), VERIFICADA com WebFetch
- body: PT-BR prático — o que é, ONDE clicar (rótulos reais pt_br: "Ativar edição", "Adicionar uma atividade ou recurso", "Participantes", "Configurações", "Mais"), tarefas comuns, erros/dicas. 6–14 linhas curtas, \n entre linhas, máx ~120 palavras.

REGRAS:
- Moodle GENÉRICO (não invente coisas da UnB). Rótulos pt_br padrão. Verifique TODAS as URLs.
- Responda APENAS com um array JSON válido (de [ a ]), SEM cercas, SEM texto extra.

TÓPICOS (visão do PROFESSOR):
1. Configurar o curso — Ativar edição, configurações do curso (formato de tópicos/semanal, nº de seções), editar/ocultar/mover seções e atividades, resumo do curso. (base: /en/Course_settings e /en/Course_homepage)
2. Adicionar atividades e recursos — "Ativar edição" → "Adicionar uma atividade ou recurso"; recursos (Arquivo, Pasta, Página, URL, Livro, Rótulo) vs atividades; mover/recuar/duplicar/excluir. (base: /en/Activities e /en/Resources)
3. Matricular usuários (Participantes) — menu Participantes, "Inscrever usuários", métodos de inscrição (manual, autoinscrição com chave de inscrição, coorte), papéis (aluno/professor), remover/suspender. (base: /en/Enrolment e /en/Add_students)
4. Grupos e agrupamentos — criar grupos, criação automática, agrupamentos, modos de grupo (visíveis/separados) e como aplicar em atividades. (base: /en/Groups e /en/Groupings)

# Moodle Course Settings Configuration

**Page Confirmation:** This page exists as "Course settings" in MoodleDocs (version 5.2 docs), accessible via Course navigation.

## Key Configuration Steps

### Accessing Settings
Users with appropriate permissions navigate to "Course navigation > Settings" to modify course parameters.

### Core Format Settings
The documentation describes selecting a course format under the "Course format" section. Available options mentioned include:
- Weekly format
- Topics format
- Social format

The page references "Course formats" for additional details but doesn't enumerate all format options with specific UI labels.

### Course Structure
For layout configuration, the page notes: "Teachers choose from the dropdown whether they wish to 'show all sections on one page' in the familiar scrolling format, or 'show one section per page'."

### Course Summary
Under the Description section, users configure the course summary, which appears on course listing pages and is searchable.

## Notable Omissions
The documentation doesn't provide specific UI button labels for "turning editing on" or exact counts for section configuration. These features are referenced elsewhere in Moodle's documentation hierarchy rather than detailed on this settings page itself.

# Course Homepage Editing Summary

**Page Confirmation:** The page exists and is titled "Course homepage" in MoodleDocs (Moodle 5.2 documentation).

## How to Edit a Course Homepage

**Enable Edit Mode:**
Start by toggling edit mode on using "the Edit mode toggle" button visible at the top of the course page.

**Edit Sections:**
- Rename sections using "the pencil icon"
- Access section menus via "the three dots to the right of the section name"
- From these menus, you can: Duplicate, move, get a permalink, or view individual sections

**Modify Activities/Resources:**
- Drag and drop items to reorder them
- Use the three-dot action menu to access "Availability" options, allowing you to show, hide, or make items available without displaying them
- Indent activities by moving them "once to the right"

**Bulk Editing:**
Click "Bulk actions" near the top right to select multiple items and apply changes like availability, duplication, moving, or deletion.

**Add Content:**
Click anywhere on the course to open "the Activity chooser" for adding new sections and activities.

**Key UI Labels Used:** "Edit mode toggle," "three dots," "Bulk actions," "Add week," "Activity chooser," "Availability"

# Moodle Activities Page Summary

**Page Confirmation:** The page titled "Activities" exists on MoodleDocs (version 5.2 documentation).

## How to Add an Activity

To add an activity, turn on editing in your course and click the link labeled **"Add an activity or resource."**

## Activity Types

Moodle's standard installation includes 15 different activity types:

1. Assignments
2. BigBlueButton
3. Choice
4. Database
5. Feedback
6. Forum
7. Glossary
8. H5P activity
9. Lesson
10. LTI External tool activity
11. Quiz
12. SCORM
13. Wiki
14. Workshop
15. (Additional plugins available from the Moodle plugins directory)

## Key Definition

"An activity is a general name for a group of features in a Moodle course. Usually an activity is something that a student will do that interacts with other students and or the teacher."

The page distinguishes activities from Resources, noting that activities are features students contribute to directly, whereas Resources are teacher-presented content.

# Moodle Resources Page Summary

**Page Confirmation:** Yes, this page exists. Title: "Resources" (MoodleDocs 5.2)

## Resource Types Overview

The documentation describes seven resource types teachers can add to courses:

1. **Book** - "A multi-page resource in a book-like format, with chapters and subchapters."
2. **File** - Supports various formats; displays within the course or prompts download when necessary.
3. **Folder** - Organizes files; can contain nested folders.
4. **IMS Content Package** - Imports static materials in standard IMS format.
5. **Page** - Instructor-created web pages using the text editor.
6. **Text and Media Area** - Displays textual and multimedia content directly on course pages.
7. **URL** - Provides web links as course resources.

## How to Add Resources

The page specifies: *"In edit mode, a teacher can add resources via the 'Add an activity or resource' link."* This is the exact UI label referenced in the documentation.

Resources display as single links with icons indicating their type.

content.content:
# Moodle Enrolments Page Summary

**Page Confirmation:** Yes, this page exists. The actual title is "Enrolments" (located at docs.moodle.org/502/en/Enrolments).

## Enrolment Methods Covered

The documentation describes enrolment as "the process of marking users as participants in the course, in other words assigning them a role such as student or teacher."

Three key methods mentioned:

1. **Manual Enrolment** - "the administrator or course teacher adds users manually"
2. **Self Enrolment** - "a user can choose to enrol him/herself into a course"
3. **Cohort Sync** - "users are part of a Cohort which is added to the course"

## Limitations

The provided page content does **not include**:
- Details about self-enrolment with enrolment keys
- Information on the Participants menu
- Instructions for enrolling users
- Role assignment procedures
- Suspension or user removal processes
- Exact UI labels

The page functions as an overview/index linking to detailed documentation on these topics rather than providing step-by-step implementation details. For comprehensive guidance on enrolment management, the documentation directs readers to specific plugin pages and related resources like "Course enrolment" and "Enrolment FAQ."

# Course Enrolment Page Summary

**Page Confirmation:** The page exists with the actual title "Course enrolment" (hosted at MoodleDocs, version 5.2).

## Adding Students via Participants

According to the documentation, teachers can manually enrol students by accessing the nav drawer and selecting **Participants**, then clicking **'Enrolled users'** in the gear menu. Alternatively, navigate to "Course administration > Users" in the Administration block if using a non-Boost theme.

The page notes that "Manual enrolment" must be enabled for teachers to add students this way. When this method is active, "teachers may add students to their course from the nav drawer Participants link."

## Regarding Roles

The documentation does **not** explain assigning roles as a method to add students to courses. Instead, it references a separate concept: "Other users" — individuals "assigned a role in a course without enrolling them" — indicating role assignment is distinct from the enrolment process.

## Key Methods Listed

The page outlines several enrolment approaches:
- Self enrolment (student-initiated signup)
- Manual enrolment (teacher-added)
- Bulk enrolments (CSV file uploads by administrators)
- Cohort sync
- Course meta linking
- PayPal enrolment

# Moodle Groups Summary

**Page Confirmation:** Yes, this page exists. The actual title is "Groups" from MoodleDocs (Moodle 5.2 documentation).

## Creating Groups

To create a group, click the "Create group" button via one of these paths:
- Using Boost theme: Select "Participants" from course navigation, then choose "Groups" from the dropdown
- Using Classic theme: Navigate to "Administration > Course administration > Users > Groups"

Then add a group name, optional description, enrolment key, and picture. Enable "Enable group messaging" if desired, then click "Save changes." Finally, select the group and click "Add/remove users" to assign participants.

## Auto-Create Groups

The "Auto-create groups" button allows automatic group generation using a naming scheme where "#" creates sequential numbers (Group 1, 2, 3) and "@" creates letters (Group A, B, C). You can specify either a number of groups or members per group. The "Prevent last small group" option avoids creating undersized final groups by redistributing members.

## Group Modes

Three modes exist:
- **No groups:** Everyone in one community
- **Separate groups:** Groups cannot see others
- **Visible groups:** Groups work separately but see others' work (read-only)

## Access Point

Via Participants menu: Select "Participants" from course navigation, then "Groups" from the dropdown menu.

# Groupings Documentation Summary

**Page Confirmation:** The page exists with the exact title "Groupings" on MoodleDocs (Moodle 5.2 documentation).

## What Groupings Are

"A grouping is a collection of groups within a course." This feature enables educators to organize multiple groups for collaborative work on shared tasks.

## Creating Groupings

Navigate to the course and select the _Groupings_ option in the _Participants_ drop-down menu, then choose _Create grouping_. You'll enter:
- _Grouping name_ (required)
- _Grouping ID number_ (optional, for external system matching)
- _Grouping description_ (optional)

## Adding Groups to Groupings

1. Select _Groups_ in the _Participants_ drop-down
2. Click the "Show groups in grouping" people icon
3. Select groups from the "Potential members" list
4. Click the arrow button to move them to "Existing members"
5. Click "Back to groupings"

## Applying to Activities

1. Click _Edit settings_ for an activity
2. In Common module settings, set a group mode
3. Select your grouping from the grouping dropdown menu
4. Click "Save changes"

When set to separate groups mode, students only see their assigned activities, and teachers see the grouping name in brackets after the activity on the course page.

# Page Confirmation and Summary

**Page Exists:** Yes, this is an official MoodleDocs page titled "Manual enrolment" from the Moodle 5.2 documentation.

## How Teachers Enrol Users via Participants

According to the documentation, the primary method involves these steps:

1. Navigate to **Participants** from the course navigation menu
2. Click the **'Enrol users' button** located at the top or bottom right of the page
3. Use the dropdown to assign a specific role if needed
4. Expand options by clicking 'Show more' to configure settings
5. Search or browse for users via the selection dropdown
6. Click the desired user to select them
7. Finally, click **'Enrol selected users and cohorts'** to complete enrollment

The documentation notes that "enrolment options include the option to add the user to a group and to choose a starting from date." Teachers can also edit individual enrollment start and end dates afterward through the edit icon in the enrolment methods column.

# Enrolment Methods Page Confirmation

**Page Exists:** Yes

**Actual Title:** "Enrolment methods" (from MoodleDocs, Moodle 5.2 documentation)

## Enrolment Methods Covered

The page documents six primary enrollment approaches:

1. **Manual enrolment** - Teachers enroll users individually via "Course administration > Users > Enrolled users"
2. **Self enrolment** - Users join directly or with an enrolment key; supports multiple instances with different roles
3. **Guest access** - Allows viewing without participation; optional key-protected entry
4. **Cohort sync** - Administrator/manager-only method linking pre-defined user groups
5. **Course meta link** - Automatic enrollment when users join linked courses
6. **PayPal** - Payment-based enrollment requiring administrator setup

## Managing Methods

According to the documentation, managers and teachers access enrollment settings by navigating to "Participants link then selecting 'Enrolment methods' from the dropdown menu." From there, users can:

- Add new methods via dropdown selection
- Delete unused methods using the X icon
- Toggle visibility with an eye icon while preserving settings
- Reorder self-enrollment options with arrow controls
